rules.summary: A code comment describes the code; it does not argue about it.
rules.why: A description stays true for as long as the code does. An argument is written to persuade a reader at one moment, and the debate it answers is not in the file, so it rots immediately and misleads whoever reads it next. Comments that rehearse a decision, editorialise about quality, or address the reader rhetorically outlive the discussion that produced them.
allowedFixes: State what the code does, in the fewest words that are accurate.
State a constraint the reader cannot infer from the code, such as an ordering requirement or an external contract.
Move the reasoning to the commit message, where it is dated and attached to the change that needed it.
Move a durable design decision to a document the code can reference by path.
Delete the comment when the code already says the same thing.

notFixes.pattern: Soften the wording while keeping the argument.
notFixes.because: The comment still answers a debate that is not in the file, so it still rots when the debate is settled.

notFixes.pattern: Move the editorial text into a TODO or NOTE marker.
notFixes.because: The marker changes how the comment is filed, not what it says; the argument is still there and still undated.

notFixes.pattern: Replace the comment with a longer one that explains the reasoning more fully.
notFixes.because: Length is not the problem. A fuller argument is more to maintain and no more durable.

notFixes.pattern: Delete the comment and leave a non-obvious constraint undocumented.
notFixes.because: This rule reports comments that argue, not comments that exist. Removing a genuine constraint trades an editorial comment for a missing one.

phrases.description: Extra phrases this repository treats as editorial, matched case-insensitively.
